from_quote: BY AND WITH THE ADVICE AND CONSENT OF THE SENATE, TO MAKE TREATIES, PROVIDED TWO THIRDS OF THE SENATORS PRESENT CONCUR
rationale: The paragraph quotes the treaty power of this clause, which it introduces as power that "the second section gives" to the President.
to_quote: by and with the Advice and Consent of the Senate, to make Treaties, provided two thirds of the Senators present concur

from_quote: they have committed the appointment of senators to the State legislatures
rationale: Says the convention "committed the appointment of senators to the State legislatures," echoing this clause's "chosen by the Legislature thereof."

from_quote: By excluding men under thirty-five from the first office
rationale: Says the Constitution excludes "men under thirty-five from the first office," which in this paragraph is the President's, the age given in this clause.
to_quote: attained to the Age of thirty five Years

from_quote: those under thirty from the second
rationale: Says the Constitution excludes men "under thirty from the second" office, which in this paragraph is a senator's, the age given in this clause.

from_quote: providing for the frequent elections of senators in such a way as to obviate the inconvenience of periodically transferring those great affairs entirely to new men
rationale: Credits the convention with providing for elections of senators that leave "a considerable residue of the old ones in place." Low because the paragraph describes the arrangement without naming the clause or using its words.

from_quote: although the President must, in forming them, act by the advice and consent of the Senate
rationale: Returns to the treaty power quoted in the second paragraph, repeating its words "advice and consent of the Senate."
to_quote: by and with the Advice and Consent of the Senate, to make Treaties

from_quote: he may at any time convene them
rationale: Says the President "may at any time convene" the Senate, echoing this clause's "convene both Houses, or either of them."

from_quote: averse to their being the SUPREME laws of the land
rationale: Takes up the objection to treaties being "the SUPREME laws of the land," repeating this clause's words "supreme Law of the Land."
